main.description: Builds an ordered GainForest activity feed from current indexed records for the registered feed and parameters selected in the request. The response contains references and selection metadata only: AT-URIs, CIDs, account DIDs, timestamps, and group counts. It does not contain record content. The caller hydrates the referenced records itself. Observations by one account and recordings in one recorder folder are folded into groupItems of at least 3 rows, even when other rows lie between them; smaller groups come back as separate recordItems. A group that continues on a later page comes back as another card with the same groupKey, which clients merge as described on groupItem. Authentication is optional and is verified when supplied, but the activity feed does not depend on the caller: the same request returns the same page whoever sends it. Omitting params selects the global feed.

errors.name: InvalidRequest
errors.description: The request or the selected feed's parameters are malformed or semantically invalid.

errors.name: UnsupportedFeed
errors.description: The requested feed identifier is not registered by this service.

errors.name: InvalidCursor
errors.description: The cursor is invalid or incompatible with the selected feed.

errors.name: InternalError
errors.description: The service encountered an internal error.

feedId.description: Identifier of the feed algorithm to execute.

params.description: Algorithm-specific parameters. Optional for app.gainforest.feed.defs#activityFeed: when omitted, its default applies (filter all).

limit.description: Number of cards to build the page from. A group is one card, but a group of fewer than 3 rows is returned as separate records, so a page can hold up to twice this many items. It holds fewer when the data or the request's row budget ends it first. The selected feed determines the default and may enforce a lower maximum.

cursor.description: Opaque cursor returned by a previous request for this feed.

schema.description: Returns ordered feed items and an optional cursor for the next page. Items are references and selection metadata, not records.

cursor.description: Cursor for the next page. Omitted when no later page is known.
